newsitem.title: CHINA: POLL - HK turns selective on China-backed red chips.
newsitem.headline: POLL - HK turns selective on China-backed red chips.

text.p: Hong Kong stock analysts are growing more choosy about China-backed red chips, focusing on companies with well-connected parents and good quality assets, a survey conducted by Reuters showed.

Asked for their top 10 picks among red chip stocks following Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1, six of 10 Hong Kong-based China analysts interviewed found difficulties in compiling a full list.
They said people had became more selective and conservative after the recent red chip euphoria boosted both the price and supply of the China-related stocks.
"I think people will become a lot more selective and they will only pick a few of the red chips that really can grow into large conglomerates," said Anthony May at DBS Securities.
Red chips surged in the run-up to Hong Kong's return to China on July 1.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliate Corporations Index has surged 28 percent since its launch on June 16 and public offers of red chip shares drew huge public responses.

Most analysts agreed that red chips, Hong Kong-based companies with financial support from Chinese parents, will continue to dominate the Hong Kong market in the second half of the year -- although gains may not be as big as the pre-handover period.
"In the second half of 1997, there still should be a bustling and exciting market for red chips," said Jeffrey Cheng at CEF Brokerage.
"If you want to play China, red chips are first choice," he said, adding that they were more transparent and flexible when compared with China-incorporated H-shares.

Asked for the criteria by which they evaluated red chip companies, all 10 analysts said the parents' backing and their connections were important, immediately followed by the quality of assets and management.
"The top priority is connections, whether they have deal-making ability for asset injections," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
Connections refer to the Chinese parents' relationships with the central government or linkages to ministries which supervise China's industries and economy.
All eight brokerages polled recommended China Resources Enterprise Ltd, which is ultimately controlled by China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.
"China Resources Enterprises has very good assets and that is on the top of all those companies (he named)," DBS' May said.

It was followed by Guangnan (Holdings) Ltd, the sole distributor of live and fresh foodstuffs exported from Guangdong province, which was picked by seven analysts. Guangnan is backed by the provincial government of Guangdong.
Getting the nod from six houses each were CITIC Pacific Ltd, Ng Fung Hong Ltd and Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd.

Salomon Brothers could not provide a list since it did not look at red chips as a category, dividing them among their respective industries, while HSBC James Capel declined to provide a list, citing the increased risk in the sector.
"The recent price rise has been a bit overdone and the risk ratio against return is too high now," said Alex Fan at HSBC James Capel.
"Asset injections are likely to continue and individual stocks should continue to attrack buyers but I will not recommend (buy)," he said.
